     1	import io
     2	import os
     3	import sys
     4	import shutil
     5	import tempfile
     6	
     7	import importlib.resources
     8	from os.path import join as pjoin
     9	
    10	from ctypes import cdll, CDLL
    11	from ctypes import Structure
    12	from ctypes import POINTER, c_void_p, c_char, c_int, c_char_p, c_bool
    13	
    14	DOWNWARD_LIB_PATH = pjoin(importlib.resources.files("fast_downward"), "libdownward.so")
    15	
    16	# Function to unload a shared library.
    17	dlclose_func = CDLL(None).dlclose  # This WON'T work on Win
    18	dlclose_func.argtypes = [c_void_p]
    19	
    20	
    21	class CapturingStdout(list):
    22	    def __enter__(self):
    23	        self._stdout = sys.stdout
    24	        sys.stdout = self._stringio = io.StringIO()
    25	        return self
    26	
    27	    def __exit__(self, *args):
    28	        self.extend(self._stringio.getvalue().splitlines())
    29	        del self._stringio    # free up some memory
    30	        sys.stdout = self._stdout
    31	
    32	
    33	class Operator(Structure):
    34	    """
    35	    An Operator object contains the following fields:
    36	
    37	    :param num: Operator ID
    38	    :type num: int
    39	    :param name: Operator name
    40	    :type name: string
    41	
    42	    ..warning this class must reflect the C struct in interface.cc.
    43	
    44	    """
    45	    _fields_ = [
    46	        ("id", c_int),
    47	        ("_name", c_char*1024),  # Fixed-length name.
    48	        ("nb_effect_atoms", c_int),
    49	    ]
    50	
    51	    def __init__(self, id=-1, name=b"", nb_effect_atoms=0):
    52	        self.id = id
    53	        self.nb_effect_atoms = nb_effect_atoms
    54	        self._name = name
    55	
    56	    def __str__(self):
    57	        return "Id {}:\t{}".format(self.id, self.name)
    58	
    59	    def __repr__(self):
    60	        return str(self)
    61	
    62	    @property
    63	    def name(self):
    64	        return self._name.decode('cp1252')
    65	
    66	
    67	class Atom(Structure):
    68	    """
    69	    An Atom object contains the following fields:
    70	
    71	    :param num: Operator ID
    72	    :type num: int
    73	    :param name: Operator name
    74	    :type name: string
    75	
    76	    ..warning this class must reflect the C struct in interface.cc.
    77	
    78	    """
    79	    _fields_ = [
    80	        ("_name", c_char*1024),  # Fixed-length name.
    81	    ]
    82	
    83	    def __init__(self):
    84	        self._name = ""
    85	
    86	    def __str__(self):
    87	        return "{}".format(self.name)
    88	
    89	    def __repr__(self):
    90	        return str(self)
    91	
    92	    @property
    93	    def name(self):
    94	        return self._name.decode('cp1252')
    95	
    96	
    97	def load_lib():
    98	    """ Loads a copy of fast-downward's shared library. """
    99	
   100	    # Make a copy of libdownward.so before loading it to avoid concurrency issues.
   101	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
   102	        downward_lib_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'libdownward.so')
   103	        if not os.path.isfile(DOWNWARD_LIB_PATH):
   104	            raise RuntimeError("Can't find: {}".format(DOWNWARD_LIB_PATH))
   105	
   106	        shutil.copyfile(DOWNWARD_LIB_PATH, downward_lib_path)
   107	        downward_lib = cdll.LoadLibrary(downward_lib_path)
   108	
   109	        downward_lib.load_sas.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   110	        downward_lib.load_sas.restype = None
   111	
   112	        downward_lib.load_sas_replan.argtypes = [c_char_p]
   113	        downward_lib.load_sas_replan.restype = None
   114	
   115	        downward_lib.cleanup.argtypes = []
   116	        downward_lib.cleanup.restype = None
   117	
   118	        downward_lib.get_applicable_operators_count.argtypes = []
   119	        downward_lib.get_applicable_operators_count.restype = int
   120	        downward_lib.get_applicable_operators.argtypes = [POINTER(Operator)]
   121	        downward_lib.get_applicable_operators.restype = None
   122	
   123	        downward_lib.get_state_size.argtypes = []
   124	        downward_lib.get_state_size.restype = int
   125	        downward_lib.get_state.argtypes = [POINTER(Atom)]
   126	        downward_lib.get_state.restype = None
   127	
   128	        downward_lib.apply_operator.argtypes = [c_int, POINTER(Atom)]
   129	        downward_lib.apply_operator.restype = int
   130	
   131	        downward_lib.check_goal.argtypes = []
   132	        downward_lib.check_goal.restype = bool
   133	
   134	        downward_lib.solve.argtypes = [c_bool]
   135	        downward_lib.solve.restype = bool
   136	
   137	        downward_lib.solve_sas.argtypes = [c_char_p, c_bool]
   138	        downward_lib.solve_sas.restype = bool
   139	
   140	        downward_lib.replan.argtypes = [c_bool]
   141	        downward_lib.replan.restype = bool
   142	
   143	        downward_lib.get_last_plan_length.argtypes = []
   144	        downward_lib.get_last_plan_length.restype = int
   145	
   146	        downward_lib.get_last_plan.argtypes = [POINTER(Operator)]
   147	        downward_lib.get_last_plan.restype = None
   148	
   149	        downward_lib.check_solution.argtypes = [c_int, POINTER(Operator)]
   150	        downward_lib.check_solution.restype = bool
   151	
   152	    return downward_lib
   153	
   154	
   155	def close_lib(downward_lib):
   156	    downward_lib.cleanup()
   157	    dlclose_func(downward_lib._handle)
   158	
   159	
   160	def pddl2sas(domain: str, problem: str, verbose: bool = False, optimize=False) -> str:
   161	    """ Converts a PDDL domain-problem to fast-downward planning task format (SAS).
   162	
   163	    Arguments:
   164	        domain: text content of the PDDL file describing the domain.
   165	        problem: text content of the PDDL file describing the problem.
   166	        verbose: display information about PDDL->SAS conversion.
   167	
   168	    Returns:
   169	        planning task described in the SAS format understood by fast-downward.
   170	    """
   171	    # HACK: modify sys.argv according to what module `options` expects.
   172	    import sys
   173	    sys.argv = ["translate.py", "domain", "task"]
   174	    from fast_downward.translate import options
   175	    from fast_downward.translate import normalize
   176	    from fast_downward.translate import translate
   177	    from fast_downward.translate.pddl_parser import lisp_parser, parsing_functions
   178	
   179	    if optimize:
   180	        # Optimize translation for faster search.
   181	        options.filter_unimportant_vars = True
   182	        options.filter_unreachable_facts = True
   183	        options.use_partial_encoding = True
   184	        options.skip_variable_reordering = False
   185	        options.add_implied_preconditions = True
   186	        options.invariant_generation_max_candidates = 0
   187	        # options.generate_relaxed_task = True
   188	    else:
   189	        # Do not optimize translation to avoid pruning operators and facts.
   190	        options.filter_unimportant_vars = False
   191	        options.filter_unreachable_facts = False
   192	        options.use_partial_encoding = False
   193	        options.skip_variable_reordering = True
   194	        options.add_implied_preconditions = False
   195	        options.invariant_generation_max_candidates = 0
   196	        # options.generate_relaxed_task = True
   197	
   198	    with CapturingStdout() as stdout:
   199	        # Load task.
   200	        domain_pddl = lisp_parser.parse_nested_list(domain.split("\n"))
   201	        problem_pddl = lisp_parser.parse_nested_list(problem.split("\n"))
   202	        task = parsing_functions.parse_task(domain_pddl, problem_pddl)
   203	
   204	        normalize.normalize(task)
   205	        sas_task = translate.pddl_to_sas(task)
   206	
   207	        # Write SAS file to a string to avoid I/O.
   208	        sas_io = io.StringIO()
   209	        sas_task.output(sas_io)
   210	        sas_io.seek(0)
   211	        sas = sas_io.read()
   212	
   213	    if verbose:
   214	        print("\n".join(stdout))
   215	
   216	    return task, sas
